messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Memory
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Threat
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Threat
  - Triggers → Memory
  - Triggers → Negative Appraisals
  - Negative Appraisals → Threat
  - Negative Appraisals → Memory
  - Negative Appraisals → Triggers
  - Memory → Threat
  - Memory → Negative Appraisals
  - Memory → Triggers
  - Threat → Triggers

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Twenty-nine-year-old Arjun’s life fractured six months ago during a late-night argument in his apartment. His girlfriend, fueled by wine and escalating accusations about his loyalty, had shoved him against the kitchen counter. In the dim light, he remembered the sharp, sour scent of her sweat, the way her voice had dropped into a specific, venomous cadence about him never being enough. When she finally grabbed his wrist and swung the heavy ceramic mug, the impact shattered the illusion of safety. He had frozen, certain he could have dodged it, and that paralysis would haunt him. Now, walking through the downtown market to restock his small spice shop, the ambient warmth carries a faint, familiar musk. That sudden waft of sweat instantly pulls Arjun back to the kitchen, the memory flooding him with unbidden clarity. The scent’s arrival does not fade; it immediately floods his nervous system, convincing him that danger is closing in once more. Because his body keeps reacting as if he is still in danger, he begins to doubt his own stability, convinced he cannot rely on himself to stay grounded. This conviction that he is fundamentally compromised turns his attention inward, making him hyperaware of every shifting voice and crowded aisle, which quickly curdles into a pervasive sense of threat. The shop’s narrow layout, once a comfort, now feels like a trap. When a customer leans over his counter to ask about card payments, Arjun flinches, his stomach dropping as if an unknown threat is closing in. This constant scanning for danger makes him hyperalert to the very cues that originally sparked the abuse. The belief that he cannot rely on himself amplifies his sensitivity to these cues, ensuring that certain conversation topics instantly hijack his attention. He starts avoiding any discussion of control or financial stress, fearing they will ignite the same violent escalation. Each avoidance narrows his world, yet it also reinforces the fear that the world remains unsafe. Over weeks, these precautions became rigid habits. He checks the shop locks three times before locking up, cancels dinner plans with his girlfriend, and spends his days counting inventory with meticulous, frantic precision. The memories do not stay confined to waking hours. When he finally retreats to his bedroom, the quiet is no longer peaceful. The sheer weight of what he did not do to stop the mug from swinging settles heavily on his chest, breeding a cold, unyielding guilt. He tells himself he will never forgive himself for not doing more, and each returning memory actively fuels his self-reproach, convincing him that his body is an enemy that will always betray him. Sometimes, without a clear image at all, he will simply sit on the edge of the bed and feel the full emotional intensity of the event, his breath shortening as if he were still there. A surge of rage on recall leaves his hands trembling, stripping away his emotional armor and lowering his threshold for danger. That lowered threshold makes certain conversation topics and familiar scents instantly provocative, while a lingering dread of strangers approaching him down the street sends his heart into a frantic rhythm. Because he interprets his own physiological responses as proof of impending harm, he stops sleeping. He finds it harder to feel safe at night than during the day, pacing the floorboards until the edges of vision blur. That lingering dread, in turn, makes him more susceptible to the old triggers, and the recurrence of the memories continuously deepens his conviction that he is fundamentally compromised. What finally brought Arjun to seek help was a Tuesday morning when he stared at the shop’s front glass, unable to turn the handle, convinced that stepping outside meant walking into the same kitchen. He is terrified that he is losing his partner and his livelihood, but he is equally afraid that he is broken beyond repair. He hopes someone can help him untangle the guilt, quiet the physical panic, and finally trust his own body again.
